# 1.2.124 - the owner's four: the GM's messenger window with its Timeline, the important notices in the middle of the screen, your own Remnant as your Truth Bullet, and a player's thread only their own

One stage ships: E124 (tools/stages.json). It carries four requests of the owner of 22.11.2026, made for the
evening's session: the GM's messenger opens its own window, with a Timeline and every player's conversation
(OWNER-124-CONSOLE; the owner: "Okno gma niech otwiera zupelnie nowe okno", and later "Przemianujmy nazwe "console" na
"timeline""); the more important notices stand in the middle of the screen with their roll (OWNER-124-NOTICES); a
Remnant a player is told they left is their Truth Bullet at once, and they see its token (OWNER-124-TRACE; the owner's
option B, "told <=> shown"); and line CORE's fix that a player cannot write into another player's messenger thread.
Built by three lines: COMM, UI and CORE, and the assembly's own commits. **E39, E40, E43, E53, E58 and E83 are not
shipped**, planned 1.2.125. E26 stays 1.3.0. From v1.2.123 (the tag) to ba294981, the assembly's last commit before
this release commit: 27 commits, 8 of them merges: 6 of the lines into the assembly, and 2 a line made of
another's branch into its own (`git rev-list --count` and `--merges --count`).

In plain words. Everything below is read off the code and the headless harness; none of it has run on a real Foundry or
at a table (## Checked).

**The GM's messenger window** (OWNER-124-CONSOLE, line COMM).
- The GM's messenger button opens a window of its own instead of the drop-down list of players. On its left: the
  **Timeline** first (Polish "Oś czasu"), then every player. On its right: the view picked.
- The Timeline holds, on top, the cards that wait for a GM's decision, from every player's thread, with their buttons;
  under them, the stream of what happens - messages, actions and events - with a filter (everything, actions only, or one
  player). It refreshes in place as things arrive, without closing and opening the window, and keeps the filter's
  choice and the focus (messenger-gm.mjs; R8650-R8655; at a table, item 875).
- A player's entry opens that player's conversation in the same window; each view keeps its own typed text (R8651). The unread badges
  are on the list.
- The drop-down roster is gone; its tests moved to the window (R299, R474, R849, R1065, R1066, R1339, R1153, R296).
- Under Stained Glass a ruling card's title read bone on bone; it reads ink now, and its first letter is no longer
  drawn in the accent colour (stained-glass.css).

**The important notices in the middle** (OWNER-124-NOTICES, line UI).
- An action's result, a Tail the target noticed, a bedroom's lock found picked, forced or breached, a body found and
  the GM's day summary now stand in the middle of the screen, larger and upright, over the windows, one at a time in
  the order they came, each until its X is pressed; a click on the card closes nothing and leaves the focus where it
  was. The rest wait behind it, counted as "+N" beside the X. They are still kept in the notice history, as the
  corner's card (notice-centre.mjs `CENTRED_NOTICES`, a closed list; popup.mjs).
- A centred action card shows its roll as its centre-piece: the Hope and Despair dice, the total, the number it had to
  beat beside it and, where that is one number, whether it was reached; a second roll smaller.
- Shut, Force the Door, Pick the Lock, Keep Watch, Dash and Tail Someone report their rolls on their cards; before,
  they said one sentence.
- Only a GM's card, or a card read by its own writer, takes the middle: a player's card never centres on another
  player's screen (`centredNotice`). The time of day, refusals, receipts, the GMs' records, the messenger and a Tail's
  later steps stay in the corner.
- Under Stained Glass the centred card is opaque: a window behind it read through its body before (the words 3.2:1
  against it; 17.4:1 on the plate now, measured in Chromium).
- A centred card tells a Despair roll's trace no more than the corner did: with a trace and without, the same card,
  byte for byte (R8675).

**Your own Remnant** (OWNER-124-TRACE, line CORE; the owner: "powinno byc to spojne z tym, czy gracz widzi
pozostawiony przez siebie remnant (token), czy nie", option B, and "niech dostaje go od razu jako truth bullet").
- A Remnant your card tells you that you left - on a roll with Hope, a critical, or in an incident you are in - is
  your Truth Bullet at once, as an Observe hit would give it (Neutral, no type recognised), and you see its token from
  then on, across a reload and on another browser. A plain Despair still tells you nothing and gives nothing
  (remnants.mjs `traceFeedback`, `noteToldTrace`; R8691).
- An incident's Remnant you can see because you were there is now named on your card too, whatever the roll; its
  leaver gets the copy, the other side of the incident sees the token as before (D11) and gets none.
- The GMs get no "say what it is" request for that copy, and the action does not wait on it. One copy per trace per
  character; a later Observe skips it. With the copy, Erase a Trace works on your own trace. A Reroll from Hope to
  Despair takes nothing back: the copy stays, as a found trace stays found.
- A copy's kind follows its trace as any copy's does: a GM's retype, a tie to the crime and Faint reach its answer
  key; an unanalysed copy goes on showing Neutral, and an Analyze reads the current kind (the owner, 22.11.2026: "Tak,
  domyslnie").
- What another player's browser can read: that the trace's token is found, as after any Observe hit, and a new Truth
  Bullet on the leaver's sheet. No field names the leaver or marks a copy as their own (scenario 73's T2).
- The cards say "You leave a Remnant behind. Its Truth Bullet is on your sheet." and the like, in both languages; the
  player and GM handbooks state the rule.

**A player's messenger thread is their own** (line CORE).
- A player could post into another player's thread from the browser's console, and a card a player wrote with another
  player's thread on it was shown in that thread. A thread now counts a card only when its author is a GM or the
  thread's own player, in every place that reads a thread, and `sendMessage` refuses another player's thread
  (messenger.mjs `threadCardAllowed`, `mayPostInto`; R8690; scenario 30's "another player's thread").

## Before installing

- **No migration clause is added** (scripts/migrate.mjs has no change in the range).
- **No setting is registered** (`game.settings.register` has no new line in scripts/). No GM store is added.
- **Language**: lang/en.json goes from 6521 to 6539 keys: 19 added (16 `DRPG.Messenger.gm.*` for the window,
  `DRPG.Popup.centre.reached` and `.short`, `DRPG.Cleanup.leftTraceKept`), 1 removed (`DRPG.Messenger.rosterTitle`, the
  roster's), 3 changed (`DRPG.Action.leavesRemnant`, `DRPG.Items.discardTrace`, `DRPG.Reroll.remnantLeft`: each adds
  that the Truth Bullet is on the sheet). lang/pl.json goes from 7610 to 7628, the same. Counted on the flattened files, v1.2.123 against ba294981.
- No glyph added (icons/ and tools/glyphs.json have no change). No console name changed (tools/api-surface.json has no
  change in the range).
- **Daggerheart**: `verified` stays 2.12.9. **Foundry**: module.json's compatibility has no change (minimum 14.364,
  verified 14.365); the owner's sandbox runs 14.370, which module.json does not name.

## Known gaps

- **Not shipped**: E39, E40, E43, E53, E58 and E83 (tools/stages.json, planned 1.2.125). E26 stays 1.3.0.
- Your own Remnant: a copy given is not taken back by a Reroll to Despair (by design). A discard's roll is not drawn by
  the GMs, so a discard's "told" is the discarder's word about their own trace, and the copy is of that trace alone.
  With no GM connected nothing is placed, so nothing is told. Whether a third player could match a new Truth Bullet to
  a newly found token by their timing is not measured; it is the same for any Observe hit.
- The centred notices: Frisk, a felt Palm or Frisk, a seen Sabotage and "you are being tailed" stay in the corner (not
  on the owner's list). Under Monokuma Legacy the card's 1 px frame lets one column of the window behind it show.
- The Timeline's label: no docs/glossary.json entry (the glossary needs a decision id; there is none for this request).
- **The local gate**: only its press part ran (## Checked); its eight parts that need a Foundry v14 sandbox did not, so
  its verdict is incomplete. Nothing in this release has run on a real Foundry or at a table.
- **Carried, not closed**: the 13 rows of audit/harness/known-leaks.json, as at 1.2.123.
